svg.title: PEG-MGF: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: PEG-MGF: what has actually been tested. MGF gene message in muscle: Rises after damage in rats and after heavy lifting in young men. Verdict: Measured. Natural MGF peptide in the body: Never isolated from cells, tissue or body fluids (2010 review). Verdict: Not found. Synthetic MGF on muscle cells: Early lab growth effects; two drug companies could not reproduce them. Verdict: Disputed. Synthetic MGF on the IGF-1 receptor: No receptor activation by short MGF or a stabilized version (2016). Verdict: No activation. MGF E-peptide in animal hearts: Better heart function after heart attacks in sheep and mice. Verdict: Positive, animals. Pegylated MGF in any study: PubMed: one record, a 2026 review saying human studies are absent. Verdict: None published. PEG-MGF or MGF given to people: No registered trial; FDA has not identified any human exposure data. Verdict: No data.
